title: Fragments on Kings
blurb: Cyril of Alexandria, Fragments on Kings: a fresh English translation of the surviving Greek fragments of his comments on the four books of Kingdoms (1 and 2 Samuel, 1 and 2 Kings), from PG 69. Cyril reads the history for what it shows about Christ: Samuel's suckling lamb is a type of Christ, Israel's demand for a king is a turning away from God's rule, David's fall shows how quickly the saints are set right, Solomon's idols show where desire leads, Naboth stands for Christ put to death on false charges, and God shields Jerusalem for his own sake.
first_english_note: No English translation of these fragments appears in the Ante-Nicene or Nicene and Post-Nicene Fathers. This is a fresh English translation made from the Greek of PG 69; no modern English version was used.

text_history.method: Fresh English translation from the Greek of PG 69.
